texts.preamble: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:56244 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
texts.facts: This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.42/2024 dated 06.02.2024 registered at the Police Station - Civil Line, District Harda for the offences under Sections 304, 308, 427, 429, 435, 436 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 5 & 9 (B) of the Explosives Act, 1884. First application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 27.08.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 31874/2024. 2. Case of the prosecution in a nutshell as articulated in the F.I.R. dated 06.02.2024 is that, the S.H.O. of the concerned police station received an information from an unknown person wherein it was informed by him that a blast took place in the factory premises of Rajesh Fire Works in which 13 persons lost their lives and 400 persons sustained injuries and several residents have suffered extensive damage. On the basis of the aforesaid information, the team of the concerned police officials went to the spot of incident and there it was informed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56244 2 MCRC-5949-2025 that various individuals had succumbed to injuries and died on the spot and dozens of persons have sustained multiple injuries. Thereafter, a preliminary investigation was conducted by the police officials wherein it was discovered that co-accused ie. Raju alias Rajesh Agrawal as well as Somesh Agrawal had been running a manufacturing unit which deals in the production of various explosive substances. During the course of investigation, it also came into light that the aforesaid accused had illegally stored excess quantity of explosive substances as a result of which, such a mishap took place therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant and co-accused persons. texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the present applicant has no connection with the commission of aforesaid offence. The applicant is not Manager of the Fire Factory and he is in custody since 11.02.2024. It is contended by the counsel that name of applicant is not mentioned in the FIR and he has been implicated in the alleged offence at later stage on the basis of statements of prosecution witnesses Sandeep Vamne, Rukhsar Bano, Toofan Singh, Mangilal and Sharad recorded u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. PW-1 Sheikh Firoz, PW-2 Sandeep, PW-3 Rukhsar Bano, PW-4 Ayushi Chauhan, PW-5 Archana, PW-6 Ravi Chandele, PW-7 Devi Singh, PW-8 Sangeeta Chauhan have not supported the prosecution story. It is further submitted that out of nearly 400 listed prosecution witnesses, only 26 prosecution witnesses have been examined in last one year. The speedy trial is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. It is submitted that prosecution is trying to take advantage of the fact that bail application of co-accused Rafiq Khan has been dismissed by Hon'ble Supreme Court but the case of present applicant is on different footing and in FIR, no specific role has been attributed to the present applicant. Charge NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56244 3 MCRC-5949-2025 sheet has been filed and the trial will take long time to conclude. In support of his contention, learned counsel has placed reliance on Shri Deepak Kumar Vs. The State, Criminal Petiton No. 3721/2021 of High Court of Karnataka, Mahadev Prasad Kaushik Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, (2008) 14 SCC 479, Ramesh Krishna Madhusudan Nayar Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2008) 14 SCC 491, Kurban Hussein Mohamedalli Rangawalla Vs. State of Maharashtra, 1964 SCC Online SC 162, Abdul Kalam Musalman & Ors. Vs. State of Rajasthan, 2010 SCC Online Raj 4354, Shamsher Khan Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2000) 8 SCC 568, Alister Anthony Pareira Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2012) 2 SCC 648, Baldev Raj Kapur Vs. State, 2009 (108) DRJ 520, Berjesh Goyal & Anr. Vs. Daily Foods (India), 2009 (108) DRJ 527, Muneshbhai Indrajit Choksi Vs. State of Gujarat & 1, 2015 SCC Online Guj 4744. On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the present applicant. 4. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the Objector have opposed the said prayer and submitted that the factory where the explosives were stored is situated at Khasra No.99 village Bairagarh and upon bifurcation, the said khasra number was given a new number i.e. Khasra No.99/1/3/4 ad-measuring area 0.004 Hectare which is recorded in the name of the present applicant and the present applicant is a relative of other co-accused. It is further submitted that on 6.02.2024, an explosion took place in factory premises of Rajesh Fire Works in which 13 persons lost their lives and 400 persons sustained injuries and several residents have suffered extensive damage. It is submitted that on the date of incident i.e. 6/02/2024, firecrackers factory was running without any valid license. The two licenses previously granted (LE-I and LE-f) had expired on 31/03/2025 and license which has been filed in this petition is tampered document. The factory was operated in a dense residential area with no buffer zone in blatant violation of safety norms. In this case, no consent to operate under the Air and Water Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4566614/ 2 Acts had been obtained leading to a clear violation of environmental regulations. It is further submitted that bail applications of similarly situated co-accused Pradeep Goyal and Rafiq Khan have been dismissed by Hon'ble Apex Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl) No. 11583/2024 and 2582/2025 respectively. It is further submitted that there have already been three prior incidents of blast at this factory but even then applicant has continued operation in the same dangerous manner. 5. It is submitted that witness Sachin Kmar in his statement recorded u/s 161 of Cr.P.C./180 of BNSS has stated that he works as a Manager in a tax consultancy run by the name of Mittal & Associates. The income tax return of the applicant/accused Abhishek for the assessment year 2023-2024 shows an income of Rs. 10,01,194/- which is said to be from the purchase and sale of firecrackers. Tax of Rs. 1,58,610 has been paid for this. It is submitted that this return shows that applicant was actively participated in running of the firecracker factory. It is submitted that present applicant was in contact of other co-accused persons for running the firecracker factory and from his possession one Vivo mobile and a register were seized in which entries of the accounts of the factory were made. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56244 5 MCRC-5949-2025 PW-4 Ayushi has supported the prosecution story.
